details: Statutory scheduling identifies the excavated courtyard villa, bath suites and spring-fed octagonal water pool.
Archaeological record identifies the nymphaeum apse, spring from the northwest, and octagonal cistern.
Operator records the 1860s lodge as two storeys, with Cotswold stone below a half-timbered upper floor.
Operator records the single-storey museum adjoining the lodge, with a stone lower wall and half-timbered brick infill.
Architect records the 2012 West Range shelter and its timber frames, untreated larch wrap, weatherboarding, shutters and limestone base.
2012 excavation report records the 34 m West Range corridor and floors uncovered below the new shelter.
The uploader identifies as Tony Grist, matching the first revision, copyright-holder release and authorship for the Nymphaeum and lodge originals.
